contention.disposition: Codex CP1 review: run once at CP2 (operator disposition); the driver changed after the first run (Fable and Codex CP2 reviews), and the operator released one more run on the final head ('Yes, run it once', #491 comment 7061791613); both results are kept
contention.finding: final head: every K2 target passed (ack p95 26.83 ms, projection p95 13.26 ms, RSS 41.9 MiB, disk 24,748 KiB, loss 0, overlap ESTABLISHED, 1,000 imports confirmed, generation 2 verified at its own head), but generation 1, started at the barrier beside the import with one production backup (Codex CP2 review 1, finding 8), failed RECOVERY_BUSY after 25.8 s: the Plan 12.11 export (Recovery._read_generation) needs every page of one read to report the same head and retries a bounded number of times; while the import commits into the same project (about 24 a second), a multi-page read of 11,000 items saw no single head in this run's attempts, so the retries were exhausted. In the first run generation 1 published at the post-import head; when each of its attempts began was not recorded. After such a transient failure is recorded, the scheduler does not retry automatically for at least 24 hours (memory_backups.Backups.run_if_due: DUE_AFTER_MS), so the backup can stay that much older; `/memory backup now` takes one at once. Retained as a miss, never re-targeted; host note: another session's test run and the Codex desktop app were running, which qualifies the measurement conditions
contention.carried_to: CP3, inside Plan 12.12 (Codex CP2 review 5 ruling): a Claude-owned blocker under #491. The repair must produce a consistent generation (entries, seal and deletion frontier, with deletion protections intact); accepting mixed heads, more retries or waiting for the import does not qualify. It needs a concurrent-write regression and a separately released frozen contention run; the 'run it once' release is consumed
